text: The white limestone was covered in shallow, precise cuts—row after row of personal names, some still legible, many crossed out with a single deliberate stroke. Others had been erased so thoroughly that only a pale scar remained in the stone. Ninsun slowed, stylus forgotten, eyes moving from line to line with the stricken attention of someone who had spent her life reconstructing lost records and was now watching the process run in reverse.

text: He did not answer. He could hear the scraping inside his own chest now, keeping time with something that was not quite his heartbeat. The wall was erasing his father's name, methodically, patiently, the way a debt gets settled by someone who has never once in their life been in a hurry to collect.

text: The statue turned toward him. This movement was different: not directional, not procedural, but attentive. It stepped between Zik and the wall, unhurried, deliberate, and then it knelt, lowering its massive carved head until the stone face hung level with his own. Its mouth opened.
